title: Alibaba’s profit triples to $9.6bn as AI cloud revenue jumps 53%
excerpt: ‘Triple-digit growth for the thirteenth consecutive quarter’: Alibaba results show AI product sales climbing as profit triples to $9.6bn.
content_html:
Alibaba’s net income tripled to 64.4bn yuan ($9.6bn) in the quarter to September, as revenue rose 10% to 271.5bn yuan ($40.5bn), the company reported on Thursday. Higher net investment income and income from operations drove the jump, Alibaba said.

Analysts polled by FactSet had expected net profit of 23.72bn yuan, The Wall Street Journal reported. Revenue beat estimates by less than 1%, according to Bloomberg, and Alibaba’s US shares slipped in pre-market trading.

“As AI monetization continues to ramp up, we will maintain disciplined investments in AI capabilities with a focus on return on invested capital while targeting to achieve positive free cash flow,” chief financial officer Toby Xu said.

Cloud carries the growth

Revenue from AI Cloud and Compute Services, which includes the T-Head chip unit, rose 53% to 61bn yuan. Recurring revenue from outside customers grew 67%. AI-related product revenue grew by triple digits for the 13th quarter in a row, reaching 17.9bn yuan.

The segment’s adjusted earnings before interest, tax, and amortisation more than doubled, up 121% to 8.8bn yuan. Its sister unit, AI Labs and Applications, home to the Qwen models, grew revenue 51%. But its adjusted loss tripled to 10.5bn yuan, which Alibaba put down to higher AI spending and the cost of running the Qwen app.

“AI-related product revenue delivered triple-digit growth for the thirteenth consecutive quarter,” chief executive Eddie Wu said.

The company also confirmed its Zhenwu V900 chip goes on commercial release in the first quarter of 2027. This week it upgraded its flagship model to Qwen4-Max.

Shopping slows, spending climbs

Customer management revenue, mostly the fees merchants pay on Taobao and Tmall, fell 5%. The e-commerce group’s adjusted earnings still rose 243%, as losses narrowed in Taobao Instant Commerce, its quick delivery service.

Capital spending rose 60% to 50.5bn yuan as Alibaba built out AI infrastructure. Free cash flow was an outflow of 34.5bn yuan, up from 21.8bn yuan a year earlier.

The Alibaba results land days after the US moved to curb remote access to advanced chips for Chinese firms. Alibaba’s market value stands at roughly $200bn, less than half its level just over a year ago, Bloomberg reported.
